container_info.description:
The Recipe Book project is a digital platform that enables users to upload, manage, and share their own recipes, as well as receive personalized recipe recommendations. The system aims to foster a community-driven environment where culinary enthusiasts can discover new dishes, organize their favorite recipes, and interact with others. The platform will leverage user-generated content and recommendation algorithms to enhance user engagement and provide tailored suggestions based on preferences and past activity.

Expected outcomes include a user-friendly web and mobile application, robust backend services for recipe management and recommendation, and a scalable architecture to support future feature expansion.
container_info.reasoning: The container is labeled as a database container but the Recipe Book project requires robust backend services for recipe management and recommendation. The environment already includes Python 3, uvicorn and common Python libraries; FastAPI is a lightweight, modern Python backend framework that pairs well with uvicorn for headless container development, is suitable for building APIs for web and mobile clients, and supports minimal dependencies and async recommendation logic. Selecting a backend platform is appropriate because this container will host server-side services that interact with databases already installed (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB) in the image.
requirements: virtualenv or venv for isolated environment (python3 -m venv .venv)
install ASGI server uvicorn (pip install uvicorn) — use uvicorn for development
minimal dependency for DB access matching chosen DB: psycopg2-binary for PostgreSQL OR mysqlclient for MySQL OR pymongo for MongoDB
optional lightweight ORM/ODM if desired: SQLModel or SQLAlchemy (pip install sqlmodel or sqlalchemy) — only if needed
basic app entrypoint (e.g., app/main.py exposing FastAPI instance)
simple run command for headless operation: uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload (omit --reload in CI)
minimal test dependency for basic validation: pytest (pip install pytest) and one basic smoke test
environment variables handling: python-dotenv or rely on container env vars (pip install python-dotenv only if needed)
avoid production components (no gunicorn/gunicorn workers, no monitoring, no Celery in minimal setup)

steps.name: environment - create venv, upgrade pip and persist venv in /etc/profile.d
steps.description: Create a workspace-local Python venv at .venv (install python3-venv non-interactively if needed), upgrade pip/setuptools/wheel inside the venv, write a small /etc/profile.d script (uses sudo) so future shells have the venv bin on PATH, and emit diagnostic versions. Create a lightweight stamp file on success to allow idempotent checks by later steps.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-book-310206-310327/Database"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
VENV_DIR="$WORKSPACE/.venv"
STAMP="$WORKSPACE/.venv_installed"
# create venv if missing
if [ ! -d "$VENV_DIR" ]; then
  if ! python3 -m venv "$VENV_DIR" 2>/tmp/venv_err.log; then
    sudo apt-get update -q >/dev/null
    sudo apt-get install -yq python3-venv >/dev/null || { cat /tmp/venv_err.log >&2 || true; echo "install python3-venv failed" >&2; exit 2; }
    python3 -m venv "$VENV_DIR"
  fi
fi
PIP="$VENV_DIR/bin/pip"
PY="$VENV_DIR/bin/python"
# upgrade core packaging tools inside venv
"$PIP" --disable-pip-version-check install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel --no-cache-dir >/dev/null || { echo "pip upgrade inside venv failed" >&2; exit 3; }
# persist venv on PATH via /etc/profile.d
PROFILE_SH="/etc/profile.d/venv_database.sh"
PROFILE_CONTENT="export VENV_PATH=\"$VENV_DIR\"\nexport PATH=\"$VENV_DIR/bin:$PATH\""
TMP_PROFILE=$(mktemp)
printf '%s' "$PROFILE_CONTENT" >"$TMP_PROFILE"
# write only if content differs
if ! sudo sh -c "cmp -s '$TMP_PROFILE' '$PROFILE_SH' 2>/dev/null"; then
  sudo mv "$TMP_PROFILE" "$PROFILE_SH"
  sudo chmod 644 "$PROFILE_SH"
else
  rm -f "$TMP_PROFILE"
fi
# create stamp for idempotency
date -u +%s >"$STAMP"
# Print versions for diagnostics
"$PY" -V
"$PIP" -V
# cleanup temp venv error log if present
[ -f /tmp/venv_err.log ] && rm -f /tmp/venv_err.log || true

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-book-310206-310327/Database"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/app" "$WORKSPACE/tests"
# app/main.py - create only if missing

  cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/main.py" <<'PY'
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()

@app.get('/health')
def health():
    return {'status': 'ok'}
PY
fi
# start.sh - create only if missing to preserve custom scripts
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/start.sh" ]; then
  cat > "$WORKSPACE/start.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-book-310206-310327/Database"
"$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/uvicorn" app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 "$@"
SH
  chmod +x "$WORKSPACE/start.sh"
fi
# Minimal requirements.txt - create only if missing
REQ_FILE="$WORKSPACE/requirements.txt"
if [ ! -f "$REQ_FILE" ]; then
  cat > "$REQ_FILE" <<'RQ'
fastapi
uvicorn
pytest
requests
# Optional DB client: add one of: psycopg2-binary OR mysqlclient OR pymongo
# Optional: add sqlmodel or sqlalchemy if an ORM is desired
# Optional: add python-dotenv if you want .env loading
RQ
fi
# .env example - create only if missing
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/.env.example" ]; then
  cat > "$WORKSPACE/.env.example" <<'ENV'
# Example DATABASE_URL; change as needed or use container env vars
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/dbname
ENV
fi
# Short README hint - create only if missing
README_SNIPPET="$WORKSPACE/README.setup.txt"
if [ ! -f "$README_SNIPPET" ]; then
  cat > "$README_SNIPPET" <<'TXT'
Order to run scripts:
1) env-001 (create venv and persist PATH)
2) deps-001 (install dependencies into venv)
3) test-001 (run pytest smoke tests)
4) validation-001 (start server and validate /health)

Notes:
- If you want the automation to include an extra DB client, set REQUIREMENTS_DB to one of: psycopg2-binary, mysqlclient, pymongo before running deps-001. Automation will NOT edit your requirements.txt in-place; it will create a merged requirements.autogen.txt for installs.
- To request python-dotenv be installed, set REQUIREMENTS_ENV=python-dotenv before running deps-001.
- Pin versions in requirements.txt for reproducible installs before CI.
- Run ./start.sh --reload for development (omit --reload in CI).
TXT

steps.name: dependencies - install pip packages into venv (merged requirements) and ensure system build-deps when needed
steps.description: Install pip packages into the venv non-interactively. If REQUIREMENTS_DB or REQUIREMENTS_ENV are set, create a temporary merged requirements file (requirements.autogen.txt) combining workspace requirements.txt and the requested extras to avoid modifying developer files. Install system build-deps (python3-dev and default-libmysqlclient-dev) when mysqlclient is requested. After successful install, create an install-stamp file to avoid redundant installs in later steps. Validate imports with robust package->module mapping (psycopg2-binary->psycopg2, mysqlclient->MySQLdb, pymongo->pymongo, sqlmodel->sqlmodel, sqlalchemy->sqlalchemy).
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-book-310206-310327/Database"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
PIP="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/pip"
PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
REQ_BASE="$WORKSPACE/requirements.txt"
AUTOGEN_REQ="$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt"
STAMP="$WORKSPACE/.venv_installed"
LOGFILE=$(mktemp -t pip-log-XXXX)
# Ensure requirements.txt exists
if [ ! -f "$REQ_BASE" ]; then
  echo "requirements.txt missing in workspace ($REQ_BASE)" >&2
  exit 2
fi
# build autogen requirements file to avoid editing developer file
cp "$REQ_BASE" "$AUTOGEN_REQ"
# append optional extras requested by automation
if [ -n "${REQUIREMENTS_DB:-}" ]; then
  if ! grep -Fqx "${REQUIREMENTS_DB}" "$AUTOGEN_REQ" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '%s
' "${REQUIREMENTS_DB}" >>"$AUTOGEN_REQ"
  fi
fi
if [ -n "${REQUIREMENTS_ENV:-}" ]; then
  if ! grep -Fqx "${REQUIREMENTS_ENV}" "$AUTOGEN_REQ" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '%s
' "${REQUIREMENTS_ENV}" >>"$AUTOGEN_REQ"
  fi
fi
# Ensure uvicorn present in autogen (env expects uvicorn in venv)
if ! grep -E '(^|\s)uvicorn(==|>=|<=|\s|$)' "$AUTOGEN_REQ" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf 'uvicorn
' >>"$AUTOGEN_REQ"
fi
# If mysqlclient requested, ensure system headers for building wheels
if grep -E '(^|\s)mysqlclient(==|>=|<=|\s|$)' "$AUTOGEN_REQ" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ "${REQUIREMENTS_DB:-}" = "mysqlclient" ]; then
  sudo apt-get update -q >/dev/null
  sudo apt-get install -yq python3-dev default-libmysqlclient-dev >/dev/null || { echo "Failed to install system deps for mysqlclient" >&2; exit 4; }
fi
# If we already installed and stamp is newer than requirements, skip install
if [ -f "$STAMP" ]; then
  echo "install stamp exists; skipping pip install" >/dev/null
else
  # Install requirements into venv; send output to logfile
  "$PIP" --disable-pip-version-check install --upgrade -r "$AUTOGEN_REQ" --no-cache-dir >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 || { echo "pip install failed; tail of log:" >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOGFILE" >&2 || true; rm -f "$AUTOGEN_REQ"; exit 5; }
  date -u +%s >"$STAMP"
fi
# Validate imports: mapping package names to import modules
"$PY" - <<'PY'
import sys,re
missing=[]
# always-required
for pkg in ('fastapi','uvicorn','pytest','requests'):
    try:
        __import__(pkg)
    except Exception as e:
        missing.append(pkg+':'+str(e))
# read autogen requirements
try:
    with open('requirements.autogen.txt') as f:
        raw=[l.split('#',1)[0].strip() for l in f if l.strip()]
except Exception:
    raw=[]
mapped=set()
for r in raw:
    base=re.split('[=<>]', r)[0].strip()
    if not base:
        continue
    # map package names -> import names
    if base=='psycopg2-binary':
        mapped.add('psycopg2')
    elif base=='mysqlclient':
        mapped.add('MySQLdb')
    elif base=='pymongo':
        mapped.add('pymongo')
    elif base in ('sqlmodel','sqlalchemy'):
        mapped.add(base)
    else:
        mapped.add(base)
for cand in mapped:
    try:
        __import__(cand)
    except Exception as e:
        missing.append(cand+':'+str(e))
if missing:
    print('Missing or failing imports:', file=sys.stderr)
    for m in missing:
        print(m, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(6)
print('dependencies OK')
PY
# cleanup
rm -f "$AUTOGEN_REQ" || true
rm -f "$LOGFILE" || true

steps.description: Start uvicorn from the venv (or global fallback) in a new session, capture PID and PGID explicitly, wait for readiness with timeout, perform an HTTP request to /health and validate JSON, then terminate by PGID with PID fallback. Skip redundant pip install if install-stamp exists. Provide logfile excerpts on failures and cleanup temporary files.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-book-310206-310327/Database"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
UVICORN="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/uvicorn"
PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
PIP="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/pip"
REQ="$WORKSPACE/requirements.txt"
LOGFILE=$(mktemp -t uvicorn-log-XXXX)
PIPLOG=$(mktemp -t pip-log-XXXX)
STAMP="$WORKSPACE/.venv_installed"
# Ensure requirements.txt exists
if [ ! -f "$REQ" ]; then
  echo "requirements.txt missing for validation" >&2
  exit 2
fi
# If no install stamp, perform install (use autogen merge to include uvicorn if missing)
if [ ! -f "$STAMP" ]; then
  export REQUIREMENTS_DB="${REQUIREMENTS_DB:-}"
  export REQUIREMENTS_ENV="${REQUIREMENTS_ENV:-}"
  # call deps script to perform install idempotently
  "$WORKSPACE/" || true
  # We don't assume the runner will re-invoke deps; to be safe, run pip install via autogen
  cp "$REQ" "$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt"
  if [ -n "${REQUIREMENTS_DB:-}" ]; then
    if ! grep -Fqx "${REQUIREMENTS_DB}" "$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt" 2>/dev/null; then
      printf '%s
' "${REQUIREMENTS_DB}" >>"$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt"
    fi
  fi
  if [ -n "${REQUIREMENTS_ENV:-}" ]; then
    if ! grep -Fqx "${REQUIREMENTS_ENV}" "$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt" 2>/dev/null; then
      printf '%s
' "${REQUIREMENTS_ENV}" >>"$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt"
    fi
  fi
  # ensure uvicorn present
  if ! grep -E '(^|\s)uvicorn(==|>=|<=|\s|$)' "$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'uvicorn
' >>"$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt"
  fi
  "$PIP" --disable-pip-version-check install --upgrade -r "$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt" --no-cache-dir >"$PIPLOG" 2>&1 || { echo "Dependency install failed; tail of pip log:" >&2; tail -n 200 "$PIPLOG" >&2 || true; rm -f "$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt"; exit 8; }
  date -u +%s >"$STAMP"
  rm -f "$WORKSPACE/requirements.autogen.txt"
fi
# Locate uvicorn binary
if [ ! -x "$UVICORN" ]; then
  UVICORN=$(command -v uvicorn || true)
  if [ -z "$UVICORN" ]; then
    echo "uvicorn not available" >&2
    exit 9
  fi
fi
# Start server in background, capture PID
setsid "$UVICORN" app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
UV_PID=$!
# capture PGID explicitly
sleep 0.2
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$UV_PID" | tr -d ' ' || true)
if [ -z "$PGID" ]; then
  PGID="$UV_PID"
fi
_cleanup(){
  if ps -p "$UV_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || kill -TERM "$UV_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    sleep 1
  fi
}
trap _cleanup EXIT
# Wait for startup
timeout=20
BODY=""
while [ $timeout -gt 0 ]; do
  HTTP_RAW=$(curl -sS -m 3 -w "\n%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8000/health) || true
  if [ -n "$HTTP_RAW" ]; then
    BODY=$(echo "$HTTP_RAW" | sed '$d')
    CODE=$(echo "$HTTP_RAW" | tail -n1)
    if [ "$CODE" = "200" ]; then
      break
    fi
  fi
  sleep 1
  timeout=$((timeout-1))
done
if [ "$timeout" -le 0 ]; then
  echo "Server did not become ready in time. Log excerpt:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOGFILE" >&2 || true
  exit 10
fi
# Validate JSON using venv python
VALID=$($PY - <<'PY'
import sys, json
body=sys.stdin.read()
try:
    data=json.loads(body)
except Exception:
    sys.exit(2)
if data=={"status":"ok"}:
    print('ok')
else:
    print('unexpected:'+json.dumps(data))
    sys.exit(3)
PY
<<<"$BODY")
if [ "$VALID" != "ok" ]; then
  echo "Validation failed: $VALID" >&2
  echo "Server log excerpt:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOGFILE" >&2 || true
  exit 11
fi
# Evidence
echo "health endpoint status: 200"
echo "health endpoint body: $BODY"
# cleanup handled by trap
rm -f "$LOGFILE" "$PIPLOG" || true
